title: Structured Output: Entities That Hold
objective: After this lesson you will be able to map model output to records via entity(), enforce validation with validateSchema(), constrain natively with useProviderStructuredOutput(), and bridge streaming via explicit converters.
why: Routers switch on categories, UIs render fields, databases store rows — all need typed records, not prose. Spring AI's entity pipeline (converters + validation switches + provider-native constraints) turns probabilistic text into reliable Java objects with retry semantics. Unvalidated parsing is the silent-corruption vector of Java AI services.

blocks.text: `.entity(ActorFilms.class)` maps output to a record; `entity(new ParameterizedTypeReference<List<X>>(){})` handles generics; custom `StructuredOutputConverter` instances plug bespoke parsing. Records carry the contract (types, bounds) that prose lacks — downstream code consumes fields, never substrings.

`validateSchema()` validates JSON against the entity schema, retrying automatically with error feedback on failure. `useProviderStructuredOutput()` sends the schema as an API-level constraint (provider support varies — check per model). Compose both on money paths; either alone where justified. Switches are independent and composable by design — combine deliberately, not maximally.

`BeanOutputConverter` (and Map/List variants) convert explicitly — including the documented streaming bridge: collect Flux strings, convert after. Converters also supply `{format}` template variables binding schemas into prompts. Explicit conversion beats implicit parsing everywhere: same converter in prompt template and result parsing guarantees shape agreement.

blocks.title: Validate the entity
blocks.note: Run it: expect ok, then bad-enum, then missing-confidence. Entity validation mirrors the switches: shape, enums, ranges — each violation named for retry feedback.

items: entity() maps to records/generics; converters bridge streaming explicitly
validateSchema (retry w/ feedback) + useProviderStructuredOutput (native constraint), composable per path
Same converter in template + parsing guarantees shape agreement

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice validator on all three entities and map verdicts. (b) Write the Triage record + entity() call with both switches for a money-adjacent path (stated why both). (c) State when provider-native alone suffices vs validation-required.
hints: Verdicts: ok / bad-enum / missing (in order) — each named for retry feedback.
Money paths compose both: native constrains generation, validation verifies receipt (defense in depth on value).
Native suffices for well-supported providers on low-stakes shapes; validation required on money/contract outputs regardless.
exercise.why: Violation naming (retry feedback), switch composition (defense in depth), and sufficiency judgment (when native alone holds) are the three entity judgments.
exercise.code: // Entity pattern: record + switches per path value + converter reuse.

quiz.q: Entity parses but values are wrong-shaped (confidence 'high'). Missing?
options: validateSchema(): schema validation with retry-with-feedback catches shape-right/wrong-typed outputs
quiz.explain: Parsing succeeds on malformed values; validation enforces types/ranges with automatic retry carrying the error.

quiz.q: Streaming endpoint needs records now. Pattern?
options: Collect Flux strings, BeanOutputConverter.convert explicitly (documented bridge)
quiz.explain: The reference bridge: aggregate then convert. Stated as workaround with upstream direction, not hidden idiom.

quiz.q: Same converter in template {format} and result parsing. Why?
options: Shape agreement guaranteed: prompt demands exactly what parsing accepts — drift impossible by construction
quiz.explain: Single converter source synchronizes demand and acceptance. Separate definitions drift into mutual incompatibility.

summary: Records via entity(), validation via switches, streaming via converter bridge, agreement via converter reuse. Probabilistic text becomes reliable objects.
